claims.claim: Complete engine with compressor and all the operators for Toyota Venza, Camry, Sienna, Highlander
claims.evidence: Witness photos show an exposed engine bay with intake/airbox, throttle body/intake component, wiring/hoses, and visible transmission/gearbox mounting area, but the engine make/model/variant, compressor presence/condition, and whether all required operators/accessories are included are not readable/confirmable from the report.

risks.risk: Engine make/model/variant may not match Toyota Venza/Camry/Sienna/Highlander requirements (wrong engine family, ECU/immobilizer mismatch, or incompatible transmission/ancillaries).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine identification plate/stamping (engine code) and the transmission code/label, plus a photo of the ECU/part number if included.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a used engine assembly with unknown compatibility (worst-case: may require additional parts/rewiring/ECU matching).

risks.risk: “Compressor” (A/C) may be missing, non-functional, or not included.
risks.proof: A close, well-lit shot showing the A/C compressor body/label and its mounting location, or a video panning across the front/side where the compressor sits.
risks.if_unproven: Price as engine-only (worst-case: A/C compressor not included or not working).

risks.risk: Completeness is uncertain: starter, alternator, radiator/hoses, ECU, wiring harness, sensors, and other “operators” may be missing.
risks.proof: A full inventory photo laid out (or a checklist photo) showing each included component with part numbers where possible.
risks.if_unproven: Price as incomplete/unknown kit (worst-case: buyer must source missing accessories).

risks.risk: Condition risk: may have internal issues (low compression, oil leaks, overheating history) not visible in photos.
risks.proof: Compression test results and leak-down test (if available), plus a short video of the engine starting/running and any fault codes from a scan tool.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven running/unknown mechanical condition.

risks.risk: Transmission/gearbox condition may be poor or incompatible (gear oil condition, shift engagement issues).
risks.proof: Photos of gearbox label/part number and a video showing it engaging properly (or proof of recent operation), plus gearbox oil condition photo.
risks.if_unproven: Price as unknown transmission condition (worst-case: transmission may need service/replacement).

risks.risk: Damage/corrosion/cracks in mounts, lines, or connectors may exist but aren’t clearly shown.
risks.proof: Close-up shots of all mounting points, visible metal lines, and connector areas; include a corrosion-focused photo set.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used with potential wear/damage (worst-case: some parts may be replaced).

proof_requests: Clear photo of engine code/stamping (engine identification) and transmission code/label.
Close-up photo showing the A/C compressor (or video panning to confirm it is present and mounted).
Inventory photo/list of every included component (ECU, wiring harness, starter, alternator, sensors, hoses, radiator if any, and all “operators”).
Compression test/leak-down results (or any test sheet) and a scan-tool fault code screenshot if it was run.
Video of the engine starting/running (even short) showing no abnormal noises/smoke and any dashboard/scan readout.
response.reason: The witness confirms it is a used Toyota-style engine assembly with intake/airbox and visible transmission/gearbox mounting area, so it can be priced at a worst-case used/unknown condition. However, compatibility, compressor inclusion, and completeness are not verifiable from the report, so the price should reflect the highest uncertainty.
